fields.Trigger: New vendor onboarding or annual sustainability program review

Automation Opportunity: - Vendor contract auto-flag if high-volume packaging vendor without take-back clause at renewal; RTI deposit auto-reconcile against vendor settlement
Controls: - CTL-06: vendor onboarding — packaging clause check; operational control: monthly RTI deposit reconciliation by DC Ops
Pain Points / Risks: - **Deposit-loss risk**: returnable crates/pallets not returned ⇒ deposit forfeited and program uneconomic; mitigated by RTI pool reconciliation (VS-111) and deposit clawback in vendor settlement
- **Adoption risk**: vendors resist returnable packaging; mitigated by top-50-vendor focus and packaging-reduction penalty leverage
System Touchpoints: - Vendor contract module — returnable-packaging clause + packaging-reduction KPI in vendor agreements (links to VS-03 vendor management; W62 contract lifecycle)
- Returnable Transport Item (RTI) module — crate/pallet pool tracking + deposit reconciliation (links to VS-111 Packaging/Pallet/RTI; W270)
- ERP sustainability module — packaging-waste-reduction metric (links to W2619 ESG; RA 11898 EPR)
Time Estimate: ~2–3 months initial program design + per-contract-cycle negotiation + monthly RTI reconciliation (~1–2 days/month network). Top-50-vendor focus concentrates effort.

steps.activity: Sustainability Coordinator designs packaging take-back program: identifies high-volume packaging vendors; negotiates returnable packaging (reusable crates, pallets) instead of single-use
Procurement incorporates packaging requirements into vendor contracts: returnable packaging for top 50 vendors, packaging reduction targets, penalties for excessive waste
DC Ops manages returnable packaging logistics: tracks crate/pallet inventory, schedules vendor pickups, reconciles packaging deposits; Coordinator reports packaging waste reduction metrics

fields.Participants: Sustainability Coord, Procurement, Finance, Recycling Vendors

Automation Opportunity: - Quarterly auto-build recycling-vendor scorecard from collection reliability + price + manifest data; auto-flag below-market rates
Controls: - CTL-450 (ensure controlled execution — Circular Economy & Recycling Analytics (PA-73.3).)
- operational: settlement accuracy — recycling revenue validated before reporting; quarterly Finance validation per store
Pain Points / Risks: - **Revenue-underperformance risk**: un-benchmarked rates ⇒ stores under-credited vs. market; mitigated by quarterly benchmarking and volume consolidation
- **Manifest-compliance risk**: recycler with poor manifest discipline exposes BuildRight's compliance record; mitigated by manifest-compliance KPI in vendor scorecard
System Touchpoints: - Vendor scorecard module — recycling-vendor performance (reliability, price, manifest compliance) (links to VS-67 vendor scorecard)
- Financials — recycling-revenue per store in P&L (links to W2619); vendor master (W287)
- ERP sustainability module — recycling revenue trend dashboard
Time Estimate: ~2–3 days/quarter review + 1 week optimization + Finance batch. Network recycling revenue ≈ PHP 2–10K/store/mo × 200 ≈ PHP 4.8–24M/yr.

steps.activity: Sustainability Coordinator reviews recycling vendor performance: collection reliability, pricing competitiveness, manifest compliance; benchmarks against market rates
Coordinator optimizes recycling revenue: consolidates volumes across nearby stores for better pricing, negotiates volume-based rate increases, explores higher-value recycling streams
Finance tracks recycling revenue per store: PHP 2K–10K/month; includes in store P&L; Coordinator reports network-wide recycling revenue trend quarterly

fields.Participants: Sustainability Coord, Category Manager, Marketing, VP Merchandising
fields.Trigger: Sustainability initiative or customer demand signal

Automation Opportunity: - Demand-signal scan to surface circular-economy opportunities; pilot-store sales-lift auto-report vs. control cluster
Controls: - CTL-450 (ensure controlled execution — Circular Economy & Recycling Analytics (PA-73.3).)
- Operational control: substantiation file required before 'Green Choice' label activation (links to VS-22 regulatory; DTI consumer protection)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Cannibalization risk**: recycled-content SKU cannibalizes higher-margin standard SKU without incremental demand; mitigated by pilot-at-10–20-stores evaluation and margin analysis at step 2
- **Greenwashing risk**: unsubstantiated 'Green Choice' claims risk DTI consumer-protection exposure; mitigated by substantiation/certification requirement before labeling
System Touchpoints: - Item master / PIM — circular-economy attribute + 'Green Choice' label (links to VS-01 merchandise; W50 PIM; VS-78 green building advisory)
- Assortment/space module — pilot store-cluster allocation (links to VS-55 planogram/space)
- Marketing/campaign module — 'Green Choice' campaign execution (links to VS-14 marketing)
Time Estimate: ~quarterly ideation + 1–2 months/initiative evaluation + ongoing marketing. Low volume, strategic.

steps.activity: Sustainability Coordinator identifies circular economy product opportunities: recycled-content products, refill stations, product-as-a-service models, upcycled product lines
Category Manager evaluates product viability: supplier sourcing, demand assessment, margin analysis, shelf space allocation; pilot at 10–20 stores
Marketing promotes circular economy messaging: 'BuildRight Green Choice' labeling, in-store educational displays, social media content, customer DIY workshops using reclaimed materials

fields.Frequency: Daily at stores with garden centers; ~80 stores
fields.Participants: Garden Center Supervisor, Store Manager, Sustainability Coordinator
fields.Trigger: Store with garden center generates organic waste

Automation Opportunity: - Organic-diversion auto-rollup into ESG; compost-bag SKU auto-created at finished-compost stage
Controls: - CTL-450 (ensure controlled execution — Circular Economy & Recycling Analytics (PA-73.3).)
- Operational control: weekly pile-turn + temperature log signed by Supervisor
Pain Points / Risks: - **Pest/odor risk**: poorly managed compost pile attracts pests/odors ⇒ store-experience and health risk; mitigated by weekly turn + temperature monitoring
- **Revenue-visibility risk**: compost sales untracked; mitigated by SKU-coded bag at POS
System Touchpoints: - ERP sustainability module — organic-waste diversion volume + compost sales (links to W2619 ESG)
- Inventory module — compost-bag SKU at PHP 50–100 (catch-weight; links to W463)
- Garden center / nursery module (links to VS-07 store operations)
Time Estimate: ~15–20 min/store/day collection + 30 min/week composting × ~80 composting-program stores ≈ ~1,200–1,600 staff-min/day; quarterly rollup ~1 day.

steps.activity: Garden Center Supervisor collects organic waste: dead plants, soil, leaves, trimmings; separates from general waste; stages in composting area or bags for community garden donation
Supervisor manages on-site composting: turns pile weekly, monitors temperature, processes into compost in 8–12 weeks; bags finished compost for sale at PHP 50–100 per bag
Sustainability Coordinator tracks organic waste diversion across garden center stores: composting volume, compost sales revenue; includes in ESG report

fields.Participants: Store Manager, Cashier, Marketing, Sustainability Coordinator
fields.Trigger: Daily POS operations or sustainability campaign

workflows.name: Customer Reusable Bag & Packaging Reduction Program

Automation Opportunity: - Location-aware POS auto-apply correct LGU plastic-bag fee from tax master; auto-remit fee per LGU schedule
Controls: - CTL-450 (ensure controlled execution — Circular Economy & Recycling Analytics (PA-73.3).)
- operational: statutory fee remittance accuracy; monthly LGU-fee remittance reconciliation per location
Pain Points / Risks: - **LGU-compliance risk**: ~200 locations across LGUs with differing plastic-bag ordinances ⇒ fee mis-collection and LGU fine exposure; mitigated by LGU-specific fee configuration in tax master (W293) per location
- **Friction risk**: bag fee annoyances at checkout harm NPS; mitigated by reusable-bag alternative and loyalty free-bag promo
System Touchpoints: - POS — reusable-bag SKU (PHP 25–50) + plastic-bag fee (PHP 2) tender line with LGU-ordinance tax code (links to VS-08 POS; W5B in-store selling)
- ERP sustainability module — plastic-bag count + reduction trend; LGU-ordinance fee remittance (links to VS-76 multi-LGU compliance)
- Loyalty module — free-bag promo for members (links to VS-13)
Time Estimate: Per-transaction (~seconds) absorbed at POS + quarterly campaign design + monthly reporting. Volume: 2.8M monthly transactions × plastic-bag rate.

steps.activity: Cashier implements reusable bag program: offers BuildRight-branded bags (PHP 25–50 each), charges PHP 2 per plastic bag per local ordinance, encourages BYO bag; tracks in POS
Marketing designs seasonal reusable bag campaigns: limited editions, trade professional heavy-duty bags, loyalty member free bag promotions
Sustainability Coordinator reports bag program impact: plastic bag reduction (target: 20% YoY), reusable bag sales, LGU ordinance compliance across 200 locations

fields.Participants: Sustainability Coord, COO, CFO, ESG Committee

workflows.name: Corporate Waste Reduction Target & ESG Reporting

Automation Opportunity: - Auto-build GRI 306 disclosure from the per-store waste ledger with cross-check to disposal-cost and recycling-revenue data; variance exceptions flagged
Controls: - CTL-450 (ensure controlled execution — Circular Economy & Recycling Analytics (PA-73.3).)
- operational: reporting accuracy (W2612 audit trail); CFO sign-off before external publication
Pain Points / Risks: - **Disclosure-accuracy risk**: ESG/GRI 306 misstatement from poor upstream waste data ⇒ greenwashing/regulatory exposure; mitigated by CFO/VP validation (step 2) and the W2612 audit + VS-25 ESG assurance
- **Target-miss risk**: public targets missed ⇒ reputational risk; mitigated by monthly W2605 tracking and mid-year corrective action
System Touchpoints: - ERP sustainability / BI module — annual waste-metric rollup (GRI 306) from the per-store ledger (W2598–W2605, W2606–W2610) (links to VS-25 ESG; VS-28 analytics)
- Reporting/disclosure module — GRI 306 + SEC sustainability report (links to VS-17 R2R external reporting)
- ESG metrics master (W406) — emission factors and intensity denominators
Time Estimate: ~2–3 weeks annual compilation + validation + disclosure. This workflow is the annual rollup of the entire VS-73 waste-data chain; its integrity depends on upstream W2598–W2618 quality.

steps.activity: Sustainability Coordinator compiles annual waste reduction metrics: total waste generated, diversion rate, recycling revenue, hazardous waste, carbon emissions avoided, waste intensity per sqm
CFO and COO review waste metrics vs. targets; validates data; Coordinator prepares external ESG disclosure per GRI Standards (Waste 306)
Coordinator publishes in annual sustainability report; submits to SEC if required; presents to ESG Committee; sets next-year targets

fields.Participants: Marketing Mgr, Sustainability Coord, Store Managers, LGU, Schools

Automation Opportunity: - Event-registration + loyalty-points auto-issue via mobile; impact dashboard auto-built from participation + media-monitoring data
Controls: - CTL-450 (ensure controlled execution — Circular Economy & Recycling Analytics (PA-73.3).)
- Operational control: event budget approval + post-event impact report (links to VS-21 marketing-spend audit W364)
Pain Points / Risks: - **ROI-opacity risk**: community events incur cost without measurable ROI; mitigated by impact measurement (participation, media, social) at step 3
- **Partner-dependency risk**: LGU/school partner dropout; mitigated by multi-partner relationships
System Touchpoints: - Loyalty module — bonus-points issuance for participation (links to VS-13)
- Marketing/campaign module — event execution + impact measurement (links to VS-14)
- ERP sustainability module — community-recycling volume feeds ESG social-impact (links to W2619; VS-25 CSR W194)
Time Estimate: ~1–2 weeks/event design + 1 day/event hosting × ~quarterly × 200 stores (subset participating) + post-event reporting.

steps.activity: Marketing and Sustainability Coordinator design community recycling program: quarterly 'BuildRight Recycles Day' — accept paper, plastic, e-waste; partner with LGU and schools; educational workshops
Store Managers host events: set up collection stations, coordinate with recycling vendors, staff information booths, distribute educational materials; Loyalty offers bonus points for participation
Marketing measures program impact: participation count, waste collected, media coverage, social engagement; Coordinator includes in annual ESG report; recognizes top stores

fields.Participants: Sustainability Coord, Facilities, COO, External Consultant

Automation Opportunity: - Feasibility-study → capex-request auto-template with ROI model; pilot-result dashboard feeding scale/sunset decision
Controls: - CTL-450 (ensure controlled execution — Circular Economy & Recycling Analytics (PA-73.3).)
- operational: capex approval tiers on scale-up decisions; pilot ROI validation gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **White-elephant risk**: pilot approved on weak ROI ⇒ stranded capex; mitigated by CFO/COO business-case gate and scale-only-on-success discipline

- **Overlap risk**: waste-to-energy overlaps VS-108 (own renewable generation) scope; mitigated by clear boundary — VS-73 owns waste-feedstock conversion, VS-108 owns grid-interactive generation assets
System Touchpoints: - Capex/project module — feasibility + business case + pilot capex (links to VS-40 capex; VS-112 PMO; VS-108 renewable energy for own-generation overlap)
- ERP sustainability module — pilot results + ESG carbon-avoidance reporting (links to W2619; VS-25)
Time Estimate: ~2–3 months feasibility + 1 month business case + 6–12 months pilot (if approved). Low frequency, strategic; ~annual evaluation.

steps.activity: Sustainability Coordinator evaluates waste-to-energy potential: anaerobic digestion for organic waste, biomass boiler for wood waste, solar panel waste recycling; engages consultant for feasibility study
For feasible projects: Coordinator develops business case with ROI; presents to CFO and COO for approval
For approved pilots: manages implementation, tracks results, reports to COO; scales successful pilots; documents for ESG reporting
